visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 at least depicts the archer, launch angle, component/trajectory ideas and parabolic motion in roughly relevant places despite some wrong labels/numbers, while Lesson 2 is sustainedly visually broken/static with a large irrelevant triangular shape, no proper projectile arc or component construction, and only a late correct range label.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a well-formed fill-in gate with a real prompt, accepted answers, feedback, and wiring after a specific act, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functional checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has clear, natural narration with appropriately spoken math and no obvious defects, while Lesson 1 contains garbled/unnatural phrases like “1 9.8,” “0 verts,” “X2,” and repeated/awkward wording that would make the audio less clear.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed cues that generally occur close to the narration moments that introduce the vector, decomposition, vertical/horizontal focus, and range result, whereas Lesson 1 has no beat or cue timing data at all, making its visual-narration synchronization unverifiable and effectively weaker on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is more conceptually complete and pedagogically sequenced, explicitly stating assumptions, separating vertical time-finding from horizontal range, and framing the kinematic equation and range formula, while Lesson 1 is mathematically correct but terse, transcript-glitched, and relies on symmetry without as much explanation of conditions or equations.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a much more polished, centered, visually consistent animated presentation despite a few garbled formula artifacts, whereas Lesson 2 is dominated by visible player UI, off-center static layouts with huge empty space, tiny/dim text, and cluttered duplicated elements near the end.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 wins overall because four of the six dimension agents favored it, and those votes carried high confidence, especially interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and conceptual accuracy. Lesson 2 appears to have a functional interactive checkpoint, clearer narration, better timed cue alignment, and a more complete pedagogical treatment of projectile motion. Lesson 1 was preferred for visual accuracy and polish, including a more coherent animated presentation, but those strengths are outweighed by Lesson 2's stronger instructional structure and high-confidence advantages across more dimensions.
